Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

jaxR 0.1.0

First release. jaxR brings the programming model of JAX to R: functions written with jaxR arrays can be differentiated, vectorized and compiled by XLA. The reference for behavior is JAX 0.12.0.1 on the CPU; the test suite compares results against values produced by that version.

Transformations

  • Automatic differentiation in forward and reverse mode: grad(), value_and_grad(), jvp(), vjp(), linearize(), linear_transpose(), jacfwd(), jacrev() and hessian(), composable to any order.
  • Vectorization with vmap(), including in_axes, out_axes, named axes and the collective operations of lax under a named axis.
  • Staging and compilation: make_jaxpr(), jit() with static arguments, eval_shape(), and the ahead of time stages $trace(), $lower() and $compile().
  • Custom derivatives (custom_jvp(), custom_vjp(), custom_gradient()), custom batching rules (custom_vmap()), and rematerialization with checkpoint() and its policies.
  • Pytrees: nested lists and registered classes work as structured arguments and results of every transformation (tree_map(), tree_flatten(), register_pytree_node() and the tree_util functions with key paths).

Arrays and numerical libraries

  • jnp_*: the jax.numpy interface, with broadcasting, type promotion, weak types, indexing and indexed updates (at_set(), at_add() and related functions), linear algebra (jnp_linalg_*), FFTs (jnp_fft_*), ufunc objects and the extended dtypes (bfloat16, float8 variants, 2 and 4 bit integers).
  • lax_*: the primitives of jax.lax, including convolutions, windowed reductions, scatter and gather, sorting, special functions, linear algebra decompositions, and structured control flow (lax_cond(), lax_switch(), lax_while_loop(), lax_fori_loop(), lax_scan(), lax_map(), lax_associative_scan()), all differentiable and compilable.
  • random_*: counter based random numbers with typed and raw keys, the threefry and rbg generators, and the samplers of jax.random. Bits agree with JAX for equal keys.
  • scipy_*: special functions, statistical distributions, linear algebra, signal processing, FFTs, spatial rotations, interpolation, integration, optimization (scipy_optimize_minimize() with BFGS and L-BFGS) and sparse iterative solvers.
  • nn_*: activation functions, attention, normalization helpers and parameter initializers of jax.nn.
  • stax_* and optimizers_*: the neural network layers and optimizers of jax.example_libraries.
  • experimental_*: sparse arrays (BCOO, BCSR, COO, CSR and CSC formats, sparse linear algebra and the sparsify transformation), checkify, Taylor mode differentiation (experimental_jet_jet()), ODE integration (experimental_ode_odeint()), layouts, executable serialization, the persistent compilation cache and stateful random generators.

Runtime and interoperability

  • Programs are lowered to StableHLO and compiled and executed by XLA through the PJRT C API. The CPU runtime is installed once with install_pjrt(); prebuilt runtimes cover Linux and macOS on x86-64 and arm64. Any PJRT plugin can be selected with the JAXR_PJRT_PLUGIN environment variable. No Python installation is needed.
  • Host callbacks (pure_callback(), io_callback(), debug_callback(), debug_print()) run R functions from compiled programs, with ordered effects.
  • Foreign function calls into native code through the XLA FFI (ffi_call(), ffi_register_target()), with LAPACK kernels provided by R’s LAPACK.
  • Configuration (jax_config_update(), enable_x64()), transfer guards, debugging flags for NaNs and infinities, key reuse checking, monitoring events and live array inspection.
  • Expressions of the symcompR package can be compiled and differentiated (jax_lambdify(), and grad() on symbolic expressions).

Documentation

  • Vignettes cover getting started, transformations, the jnp and lax interfaces, pytrees, random numbers, SciPy functions, sparse arrays, neural networks, advanced topics (custom rules, control flow, compilation stages and callbacks), symbolic computation, and the differences from JAX.

Known limitations

  • Results are tested on the CPU. Other PJRT plugins (for example CUDA) can be loaded, but they are untested, and the LAPACK based lowerings exist for the CPU only.
  • There is no prebuilt runtime for Windows; the package installs there and needs JAXR_PJRT_PLUGIN to name a PJRT plugin built for Windows.
  • The scope is the single device, single process functionality of JAX: pmap, sharding, shard_map and distributed execution are not ported (the named axis collectives work under vmap()). Neither are DLPack, jax.export, the profiler and Pallas. Buffer donation (donate_argnums) and the unroll option of lax_scan() are accepted and ignored.
  • A few results deliberately differ from JAX where its formulas lose accuracy or misreport success: scipy_stats_norm_logpdf() at extreme scales, the bracket test of scipy_optimize_line_search(), the derivatives of padded sparse storage, the index clamp of lax_switch() for wide integers, and NaN from experimental_ode_odeint() when its step budget runs out. The differences vignette lists these and every other intentional difference.
